summary: Describes the Ipsilon Flow Management Protocol, which lets a node tell a neighboring node to attach a layer 2 label to a specific IP flow. It is informational and describes a vendor protocol.

eli5.summary: Putting a colored sticker on all the packages in one conversation so the next worker can move them along faster.

how does ifmp label ip flows
how does ifmp improve routing performance
subtitle: A protocol for labeling IP flows at layer 2.

tldr.problem: Routers process every packet by looking up its destination in a routing table, which is slow. When many packets between the same source and destination travel the same path, the routing work repeats unnecessarily.
tldr.mechanism: IFMP lets a downstream router tell an upstream router to attach a label to packets in a particular flow, so the upstream router can forward them at layer 2 using the label instead of routing them at layer 3.
tldr.outcome: Flows can be switched at layer 2 rather than routed at layer 3, improving performance. The protocol is informational and describes a vendor protocol by Ipsilon Networks rather than a standards-track specification.

facts.label: Redirection opcodes
facts.value: 5 (Redirect, Reclaim, Reclaim Ack, Label Range, Error)

today: RFC 1953 is an Informational document describing a vendor protocol by Ipsilon Networks. It has not been adopted as a standards track specification and has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: Introduction and Goals
sections.content:
The Ipsilon Flow Management Protocol (IFMP) is a protocol that allows a node to instruct an adjacent node to attach a layer 2 label to packets belonging to a specific IP flow. A flow is defined as a sequence of packets sent from a particular source to a particular destination.

The label enables more efficient access to cached routing information and allows the node to switch packets at layer 2 rather than forwarding them at layer 3. If both the upstream and downstream nodes on a link redirect the same flow, the node between them can switch the packets using the label instead of performing full route lookups, improving performance.

IFMP is designed for point-to-point links. The protocol is informational and represents a vendor protocol rather than a standards track document.
sections.eli5: IFMP lets routers tell their neighbors to put a sticker on certain conversations so they can handle them faster without looking up the address each time.

sections.title: Flows and Flow Types
sections.content:
In IFMP, a flow is identified by fields from the IP header that remain constant throughout all packets in that flow. The protocol defines three flow types, each specifying a different set of header fields.

Flow Type 0 is used to change the encapsulation of all IPv4 packets. It has a null flow identifier.

Flow Type 1 is designed for TCP and UDP, where the source and destination ports follow the IP header. It uses the source address, destination address, source port, and destination port to identify flows.

Flow Type 2 is similar to Flow Type 1 but uses only the source and destination addresses and the Time to Live field, omitting the ports.

The flow types are hierarchically ordered so that a downstream node can perform a most-specific match when determining which flow a packet belongs to.
sections.eli5: Different types of conversations have different identifying features. For example, web browsing uses ports to identify different conversations between the same two computers.

sections.title: Discovering Adjacent Nodes
sections.content:
Before IFMP can redirect flows, adjacent nodes must discover each other using the IFMP Adjacency Protocol. Adjacency messages are sent to the IP limited broadcast address using IP protocol number 101.

The adjacency protocol uses four operations: SYN, SYNACK, RSTACK, and ACK. Nodes exchange instance numbers that uniquely identify them; when a node restarts, its instance number changes, allowing neighbors to detect the restart. The protocol also exchanges IP addresses assigned to the link.

State synchronization is achieved when both nodes reach the ESTAB state. Only after achieving this synchronized state can redirection messages be sent.

A timer (typically one second) drives periodic transmission of adjacency messages, and state tables define what action to take based on incoming messages and the current state.
sections.eli5: Before routers can label conversations, they first need to say hello to each other and make sure they agree on who they both are.

sections.title: Redirecting Flows with Labels
sections.content:
The IFMP Redirection Protocol allows a downstream node to tell an upstream node to attach a label to packets in a specified flow. A redirection message specifies the flow type, the flow identifier (the actual header field values), a label, and a lifetime.

A Redirect message instructs the upstream node to attach a label to packets of a specific flow for a specified time period. If the upstream node accepts the redirect, it attaches the label to all packets in that flow using the encapsulation method for that flow type.

When a downstream node wants to stop redirecting a flow, it sends a Reclaim message to unbind the label and return the flow to default forwarding. The upstream node responds with a Reclaim Ack message confirming the label is released.

A Label Range message informs a sender of the valid range of labels it may use on a particular link. An Error message reports unsupported protocol versions or unknown flow types.
sections.eli5: A router downstream says to the one upstream: "Please put sticker number 42 on all these conversations and keep it for 30 seconds." When done, it says "Remove sticker 42 now."

sections.title: Managing Flow State and Lifetime
sections.content:
Each flow redirection has a lifetime specified in the Redirect message. If not refreshed before the lifetime expires, the association between the flow and its label is automatically discarded and the flow returns to default forwarding.

A flow is refreshed by sending an identical Redirect message with the same label and flow identifier before the lifetime expires. This mechanism prevents stale label associations if a node becomes unavailable.

If a Redirect message is received for a flow that is already redirected, the node checks whether the label matches. If the labels match, the lifetime is reset; if they differ, the flow returns to default forwarding and the new request is ignored.

The minimum time between successive Redirect messages for the same flow is one second, preventing excessive control message traffic.
sections.eli5: Each labeled conversation has an expiration time, like a warranty. If the request is not renewed before it expires, the sticker comes off.
